sections.notes:
Section 3.2 has 12 cards: 6 true (01, 03, 04, 07, 09, 10) and 6 false (02, 05, 06, 08, 11, 12). All 4 replacements keep their card's answer, so the balance stays at 6 and 6. Sections and wording were checked against the current four-section exam guide PDF. It lists 3.2 bullets for objects, lifecycle, queries, cost estimation, backup and restore, job status, Database Center and CMEK. Every source URL loaded and supports its card.

Cards that passed, with the deciding sentence:
- 01: \"ACLs are disabled, and only bucket-level IAM permissions grant access\".
- 04: \"MySQL uses binary logging as the transaction logs for point-in-time recovery (PITR)\". Since the change of storage location, the logs may sit in Cloud Storage, but they are still binary logs.
- 05: \"A backup resides in the same location as the source database\". The misconception is realistic because managed export does go to Cloud Storage.
- 06: \"You can restore from a backup to a table in a different instance\" and \"You cannot export, copy, or move a Bigtable backup to another service, such as Cloud Storage\".
- 08: \"Data displayed in Database Center is not updated in real time ... may take up to 24 hours\". This is borderline trivia, because it tests a data-freshness disclaimer rather than what Database Center does, but it is unambiguous and in scope, so it was not flagged.
- 10: \"if your bucket is located in US-EAST1, any key ring ... must also be created in US-EAST1\". The explanation's wording \"match the location\" is a slight simplification for dual-regions, but it is acceptable.
- 11: For PITR, \"The new cluster must be in the same region as the source cluster\". Cross-region backup storage exists only for on-demand and automated backups, not continuous backup, so the card holds.
- 12: The manage-backups page documents Update metadata in the console and \"gcloud spanner backups update-metadata\" to change a backup's expiration date.

No card in 3.2 rests on the same fact as a card in another section. The closest neighbours are s2.2-08 (Archive online reads), s1.2 (BigQuery billing export) and s3.1-02 (snapshot schedules), and each tests a different fact. The replacements for 02 (lifecycle age from creation time) and 09 (manual rewrite triggers the early deletion charge) were chosen so they do not give each other away. Also check that the 3 replacement true statements (99 to 105 characters) keep the section's true and false average lengths within 5 characters.

I checked all 12 cards in section 4.2. All source URLs load and are official, current docs.cloud.google.com pages. No answer is wrong. I flagged 4 cards as weak: 03 (definition), 06 (name giveaway), 09 (wording gives away the answer) and 10 (name and definition echo). The other 8 cards pass. Evidence for each:
- 01: "Each service account is located in a project. After you create a service account, you cannot move it to a different project."
- 02: "Service accounts that are created and managed by Google Cloud". Users can trigger creation of some service agents, but that does not make the false answer defensible.
- 04: Roles granted *on* a service account determine who can manage or impersonate it, while roles granted *to* it determine what it can access.
- 05: Service Account User lets a principal "attach a service account to a resource" via iam.serviceAccounts.actAs. Attaching to a VM also needs Compute permissions, but the statement only claims this role provides the actAs permission, so it holds.
- 07: --impersonate-service-account "automatically creates short-lived credentials".
- 08: "routinely rotate all keys that you manage". Downloaded keys "stay valid until you delete them".
- 11: The KSA principal identifier principal://.../subject/ns/NAMESPACE/sa/SERVICEACCOUNT. The STS token may have limits with some services, but "can grant" covers that.
- 12: "The GKE metadata server intercepts HTTP requests to http://metadata.google.internal". Pods call the same endpoint, but the GKE metadata server answers them, so False is correct.
